newsitem.title: USA: Female soldiers to recant sex harassment charges.
newsitem.headline: Female soldiers to recant sex harassment charges.

text.p: Four female soldiers are to recant allegations of sexual harassment against African American soldiers at the Army's Aberdeen Proving Ground, a local NAACP representative said.

The representative of the Hartford County, Maryland National Association for the Advancement of Coloured People, who declined to give his name, said the allegations would be recanted at a Tuesday news conference at the home of chapter president Janice Grant.
Last week, another soldier, Pvt. Toni Moreland, recanted an allegation she had been raped. She now faces court-martial charges for the recantation, base officials said.
Base officials were not immediately available for comment on the newest recantations.

The NAACP official said the soldiers who were the target of the allegations to be retracted were African American. The civil rights group has accused the military of discriminating against black soldiers in its investigation into sexual harassment in the Army.
